name: AIContentEditorAssistant
platform: Windows 10 22H2 / Windows 11 x64, with Windows Media Foundation; one standalone executable
workflow: The calling AI makes editorial decisions. ACEA does not understand a natural-language creative prompt.
Run doctor, inspect the source, then review it with timestamped contact sheets. Open the generated images with your image tools.
Inspect key moments more closely using frames or a narrower review range. Confirm the instructional stages and payoff from the footage.
Choose the shortest satisfying edit; a requested maximum duration is a ceiling, not a target to fill.
Write a version 2 job with stable clip IDs in story order, source ranges, labels, and precise effects. Validate the entire job before rendering.
Run batch, inspect output frames, and return the ordered clips plus manifest. Use batch --resume true to recover or revise.
Do not claim CapCut was edited or import-tested. ACEA generates clips for later assembly; it does not create a finished tutorial or narration.

commands.doctor: acea doctor: report native graphics and registered H.264/AAC encoders; this is a capability inventory, not proof of active acceleration
commands.capabilities: acea capabilities: this embedded interface and workflow reference
commands.inspect: acea inspect --source <video>: dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio streams, and rotation
commands.frames: acea frames --source <video> --output-dir <fresh-directory> --times <0,5,10> [--height <540>]: 1..12 PNGs, including requested and actual source timestamps; height 2..1080 without upscaling
commands.review: acea review --source <video> --output-dir <fresh-directory> [--start <0>] [--duration <seconds>] [--interval <15>]: timestamped contact sheets plus index.json; at most 240 frames, continuation_timestamp when more remain
commands.validate: acea validate --request <clip-or-job.json|->: validate all ranges, effects, source decoder negotiation, and job duration budget without rendering
commands.render: acea render --request <clip.json|->: one edited source range
commands.batch: acea batch --request <job.json|-> [--resume <false|true>]: serial ordered clip rendering, checkpoints, and manifest.json
commands.install: acea install [--replace <false|true>] [--dry-run <false|true>]: explicit per-user installation and user PATH update; open a new terminal afterward

clip_request.source: Local video path. Relative paths resolve against the request file directory, or cwd for stdin.
clip_request.output: .mp4 path in an existing directory; must differ from source

range.duration: Positive seconds; must fit source and contain at least one frame

job_request.source: One source recording for this job
job_request.output_dir: Fresh directory created by batch, with existing parent; resume requires its version 2 manifest
job_request.max_duration: Optional positive seconds. Validation reserves up to one AAC packet per clip for audio encoder padding; final manifest uses actual container durations.
job_request.settings: Shared settings; an optional clip.settings object replaces these settings for that clip
job_request.clips: 1..1000 ordered objects: {id,label?,range,effects?,settings?}. IDs: 1..64 ASCII letters/digits/-/_, unique ignoring case, excluding Windows device names. Each output is <id>.mp4.
job_request.resume: Completed output is reused only when source SHA-256, effective request, renderer version, output SHA-256, and media verification match. Reorder/relabel without re-encoding. Unmanaged output files are protected.

video_bitrate_kbps.default: 10000 at 1920x1080/30fps, proportional to resolution and fps, clamped to 2000..40000

acceleration.description: Auto prefers native GPU paths; software forces WARP rendering and software codecs. Results report actual paths and fallback reasons.

preview_height.description: Optional even height, 144..source height; preserve aspect ratio and round output to even dimensions

threads.description: Compatibility work-limit hint. Application rendering is serial; Windows components own their codec thread pools.

coordinates.target: {x,y}, each 0..1, default {x:0.5,y:0.5}; desired viewport center, clamped at edges
coordinates.rect: {x,y,width,height} normalized to the full displayed source frame, before camera movement; inside image and at least 2 source pixels
coordinates.review_cells: Contact sheets include labels. Normalize within each cell's image_rect only, excluding the label and other cells.
coordinates.zoom: 1 shows the full frame; 2 shows half the source width and height

timing.effects: Seconds relative to range.start. Half-open [start,end) intervals. Outside a camera interval, the image returns to full frame.
timing.sampling: Source-relative seconds; actual_source_time is the decoded frame timestamp, which can differ by up to a frame from the request.
timing.overlap: Camera intervals cannot overlap. Highlights run in request order before the camera. Use a single camera path for a continuous zoom/hold/return.
timing.output: Constant source metadata frame rate, supported up to 120 fps; range duration rounds down to complete frames. AAC padding may add up to approximately 22ms to container duration.

easing.curves: Quadratic; a keyframe's easing applies to its outgoing segment

effects.description: 2..32 strictly ordered {time,zoom,target?,easing?} keyframes; repeat a state at a later time to hold. Zoom must be 1..10.
Dim outside rectangular target; 0 unchanged, 1 black
Gaussian blur within rectangle, sigma 0.1..50 source pixels; neighboring source pixels contribute at the boundary

output.video: H.264 in MP4, even dimensions, square pixels
output.audio: First audio stream, stereo 48kHz AAC 192kbps; preserve timing and pad gaps with silence; silent sources stay silent
output.progress: JSON events on stderr; one final result on stdout
output.manifest: Ordered clips with labels, source ranges, actual duration, cumulative timeline_start, hashes, warnings, acceleration paths, and completion status

exit_codes.2: Input, codec, installation, or processing error

clips.label: Character creation: use observed timestamps and targets

migration: Version 1 is rejected before opening media. Use version:2; remove settings.crf and optionally set video_bitrate_kbps. No FFmpeg or FFprobe is needed.
